daphne_acme: Hey team, we flipped GCP Private Service Connect for Redwood private endpoint this morning and now our app returns TLS cert errors when calling the API. Started right after PSC attach. Can someone help?

sam_support: @daphne_acme sorry to hear that — can you paste the exact error and a minimal repro (curl or SDK request)? Also which deployment (hosted/dedicated/private) and region?

daphne_acme: Hosted API (private tenant on our VPC using PSC, region us-central1). Curl output below. We tried both via our app and from a jump host in the same VPC.
```
curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/engines/text:generate \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' 
*   Trying 10.200.5.7...
* Connected to 10.200.5.7 (10.200.5.7) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384
* server certificate verification FAILED
* CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID
* Closing connection 0
```

sam_support: That CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID usually means the cert SANs don't match the IP you're connecting to. With PSC you often resolve the service to an internal VIP — the cert will be for the public hostname. Which DNS name are you resolving locally?

daphne_acme: We're resolving api.internal -> 10.200.5.7 (that's the PSC reserved IP). Our app uses api.internal which used to be routed through Private DNS peering. After switching we see the internal IP.

ben_networks: Quick theory: TLS works if client uses the hostname in SNI that matches the cert. If you connect to 10.200.5.7 directly, curl's hostname for SNI is the IP unless you override. Try:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.com/ --resolve "api.redwood.com:443:10.200.5.7" \
  -H 'Host: api.redwood.com' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
```
This forces SNI/Host header to the public name while connecting to the internal VIP.

carol_infra: Adding to that — with GCP PSC you need to ensure your private DNS zone resolves the public hostname (e.g., api.redwood.com) to the PSC IP, not a bare internal alias like api.internal. If your clients are using api.internal, cert mismatch is expected. Two options: 1) update private DNS to map the canonical public hostname to PSC VIP, or 2) configure clients to send SNI for the public fqdn.

sam_support: Can you show output of `dig +short api.redwood.com @127.0.0.53` from the jump host and `openssl s_client -connect 10.200.5.7:443 -servername api.redwood.com`?

daphne_acme: dig returns 10.200.5.7. openssl s_client gives the cert for CN=api.redwood.com, SAN includes api.redwood.com, but when we curl without --resolve we get the invalid CN error (weird). Full openssl command output:
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = api.redwood.com
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
verify return:1
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.redwood.com
   i:/C=US/O=Redwood Inference/CN=Redwood Intermediate CA
---
```

ben_networks: The verify error num=20 suggests your jump host doesn't have our intermediate CA chain in its truststore. But your curl showed CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID which is different. Two simultaneous issues possible: 1) client trusts chain but is connecting using IP -> SNI mismatch -> CN invalid. 2) If client doesn't trust our CA, you'll see issuer errors. Are you seeing both or only the CN invalid?

daphne_acme: App logs show CN invalid. On a few hosts (older distros) we also saw unable to get local issuer. We manage images differently across fleet.

carol_infra: For fleet agents: ensure your distro's CA bundle includes Redwood's intermediate CA (we published the chain when onboarding). For the CN issue: confirm your app uses the public hostname in the TLS handshake. Some SDKs use IP if they resolve to IP then skip hostname override. E.g., Python requests uses hostname for SNI by default but if you pass an IP or use low-level sockets it may not.

sam_support: Short repro checklist for you to try and report back: 1) From a failing host run `curl --resolve "api.redwood.com:443:10.200.5.7" https://api.redwood.com -v` 2) `openssl s_client -connect 10.200.5.7:443 -servername api.redwood.com -showcerts` 3) `dig api.redwood.com` and `cat /etc/resolv.conf` 4) capture tcpdump on host to confirm SNI packet (we can help interpret).

daphne_acme: Trying 1) now — when I use --resolve it works. So that confirms SNI was the problem. Thanks.

deploybot: config-change: dns-policy updated for project acme-prod by daphne_acme at 2026-03-29T14:02:17Z

ben_networks: Nice. So long term you should: a) make your private DNS zone return the public CN (api.redwood.com) for the PSC IP; b) ensure clients use the public hostname for SNI; c) rollout CA bundle update for older hosts. Also watch for split-horizon DNS where some clients still resolve a different internal alias.

carol_infra: One more gotcha: if you use egress NAT gateways or proxy devices, TLS termination/proxying can strip SNI or change Host header. Make sure any outbound proxy preserves SNI or does TLS passthrough.

daphne_acme: Super helpful. We'll update DNS to point api.redwood.com -> PSC VIP and push CA updates to legacy hosts. Also adding a temporary client-side fix using --resolve where possible. Appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:

sam_support: Great — ping us after the DNS rollout and we'll validate. If anything else crops up (timeouts/latency once PSC in place) open another thread with packet captures and request IDs.

carol_infra: Filed internal note: PSC onboarding doc update -> add SNI and CA checklist (will PR docs). :memo:
